item.title: SCP-5113:
item.content:encoded:
Maybe my standards are low, because I can name more issues I have with this article than specific things I liked, and yet I can't say I didn't enjoy it. It's cute.

(Those issues, though, are that the pacing seems rather strange, an anomaly that regularly tries to escape did so successfully many times without explanation and without the Foundation really upping the ante, and the cat seems too easily swayed into not escaping anymore.)

Actually after I say that out loud, I think I'm gonna novote. Too cute to downvote. Too many issues to upvote. I approve in spirit but can't fully support in good conscience.

item.title: SCP-5074:
item.content:encoded:
I think the prose is rather clumsy in a couple areas. Bit too tired to do my due diligence and point them out, but I definitely think you could have written this a lot tighter. That said, uh… damn. This was really fun! Kind of a "too ambitious for me not to like it" situation, I at first thought that the link to the next offset was a link to another article, and tried not to click it so I could "solve" the article, which was pretty funny. Definitely was going to downvote that version of the article, but then the comments set me right and I experienced it in full.

Nobody is an ape with a fedora that passively gains knowledge and can write out that knowledge to be radioactive, who was taken from Wilson's Wildlife Solutions and tortured by (and subsequently escaped from) Marshall Carter & Dark. Like…

How can I not say yes? +1

item.title: Foundation Cool Achievement Badges:
item.content:encoded:
Do you plan on adding some of the ones on Roget's page? Specifically:

  • Friend Of The People — Take part in 5 writing collaborations. You must be a full co-author, not just a contributor.
  • Thousandaire — Entered into any of the X000 contests (i.e. SCP-1000, SCP-2000, SCP-3000, etc.)
  • Sharpshooter — As an author of at least 10 articles on the wiki, have an average net upvote rating for your body of work that is at least +100

item.title: Foundation Cool Achievement Badges:
item.content:encoded:
This looks fun! Off the top of my head, a few ideas for more badges:

  • Tall Tales — Published ten tales on the wiki. Individual chapters count, if they are their own pages.
  • Containment Specialist: Safe/Euclid/Keter/Thaumiel/Explained — Separate badges in each object class for posting ten SCPs at that level.
  • Canonized — Authored or co-authored a new canon.
  • Thank You For Your Cooperation — co-authored five (or 10?) pages with at least five (or 10?) different people.

item.title: SCP-5703:
item.content:encoded: I really like everything past the description, it’s a nice creepy little story with a really good event log (love the slow realization that there is no bio relationship between the “daughter” and the parents). However the containment procedures and the description don’t feel fully developed(even with the in universe WIP), mainly because the “parents” connection to the weirdness isn’t mentioned at all. But then again that could ruin the build up to the event. Either way feels a bit underdeveloped so 8/10 event log 4/10 containment/description. I feel that even with the lacking start the end more then makes up for it! +1

item.title: SCP-387: A Story Element Suggestion
item.content:encoded:
I'm not going to read all 6 pages of the discussion. So forgive me if this suggestion was already made before my post.

If granted, can SCP-387 be used for planning construction under emergency circumstance? As in if there is (For Example) a end of the world scenario in which the foundation can still re-contain everything without having to use round peg in a square hole fix. But need help with working out how to do so, using 387?

I'm speaking a bit more out of the box, but if communication can be establish with 387 and it advances far enough that 387, if left alone to their own devices, can construct a miniature version of what the foundation requires. Maybe place 387 in a time distortion location in which it's faster inside the room but regular time outside the room.

Ex. The foundation needs a mobile containment site/FOB/and-general-all-around-transportation-and-emergency headquarters made. And SCP 387 constructs a structurally sound, detailed enough, Helicarriers. With the placement of the bricks and general layout being used to help guide the construction of the life sizes Helicarrier the foundation requires to build.

item.title: SCP-3032:
item.content:encoded:
Solid concept, good execution, but the numbers are too off, that break it to me.

A velocity of 10 m/s is just 36 Km/h (less than 22.5 miles/hour), terminal velocity for a pine cone isn't much more than throwing them by hand, and the force of the explosion wasn't given. So, as far as I'm aware, this isn't nearly as dangerous as it is purported to be.

It isn't Keter, either. Even if you make it more dangerous than a modern ICBM its containment is quite reliable, and I see no reason to be otherwise. This is a solid Euclid.

You don't need to make this more dangerous. You can correct the numbers to really make it into a war-worthy missile, or you can go with the numbers and make it a freak flying tree with annoying dropping cones and a somewhat dangerous blast at the end. It works either way, if not better with the current low numbers.
